   122	## 5. The ping-pong guard
   123	
   124	Three interlocking guards stop a review → fix → review cascade.  All three must
   125	hold; each alone is insufficient.
   126	
   127	1. **Bot-commit skip (here).**  If the head commit's subject matches
   128	   `^\[(claude|codex)-(auto|review)-fix\]`, no review runs.  The regex is
   129	   `pr-review.yml:79` verbatim, and it recognises both providers and both fix
   130	   kinds.  `local/bin/autofix.sh` writes exactly `[codex-auto-fix]` and
   131	   `[codex-review-fix]` (DESIGN.md, "Fix commits").  Change either side without
   132	   the other and this guard fails open, silently.
   133	2. **The combined iteration cap (`autofix.md` §5).**  One counter across all
   134	   fix kinds, not one per kind.
   135	3. **The exclusion of sync and audit failures from auto-fix**
   136	   (`autofix.md` §3).
   137	
   138	The guard has one deliberate hole.  `pr-review.yml:69-72` says: *we only want
   139	to review human-authored pushes and the final bot-fix result (detected by
   140	iteration cap)*.  Without that exception, the last fix commit — the one that
   141	ships — is the only commit on the branch nobody ever reviewed.  So `autofix.sh`
   142	calls `review.sh <id> --force-review` once when the cap is reached — after
   143	**releasing its own fix lock** (`release_fix_lock` in `autofix.sh`), because
   144	`review.sh` refuses to run while the branch's fix lock has a live holder and
   145	that holder would otherwise be the very process asking for the review.
   146	`--force-review` is the only way past rung 7.  Do not use it to "just get a
   147	review" of a bot commit; that reopens the cascade one commit at a time.
   148	
   149	## 6. What the reviewer must return
   150	
   151	A single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state
   152	field carries no authority here (`issues-prs.md` §2): the verdict is a trailer
   153	in the agent's last message (`codex exec -o <file>`), and the contract demands
   154	three things in order:
   155	
   156	1. a `## Findings` section, one line per finding, in exactly this shape:
   157	
   158	       - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123` — one-line summary
   159	
   160	   with severity in {`blocker`, `changes`, `advisory`} and `-` in place of
   161	   `path:line` when a finding is not tied to a line; or the single line
   162	   `- none`;
   163	2. a `## Review` section with the prose;
   164	3. as the final line, alone:
   165	
   166	       VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED
   167	
   168	A missing or malformed trailer is **not** an approval: `review.sh` exits 4,
   169	posts a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and keeps the raw output under
   170	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section
   171	is discarded either — a line that does not parse is kept verbatim as a
   172	`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving
   173	verdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate
   174	still blocks.  Both rules follow the same principle as rung 5: the failure mode
   175	worth engineering against is a review that reads green without having happened.
   176	
   177	## 7. Which reviews run
   178	
   179	* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
   180	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix
   181	  collapses to one codex session; a second backend can be added by running
   182	  `review.sh` again with `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL` set, which writes a separate
   183	  per-SHA file only if you also change the file name, so treat multi-provider
   184	  review as unimplemented rather than as a one-liner.
   185	* **Prose review** only when the diff touches `blueprint/`.  On GitHub it ran
   186	  unconditionally on a cheaper tier; gating it on the diff is a local
   187	  cost decision, not a weakening — the prose prompt reviews blueprint ↔ Lean
   188	  equivalence and blueprint prose, and a diff that touches no blueprint file
   189	  has nothing for it to review.  Set `MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL` for the
   190	  cheaper-tier split.
   191	
   192	The failure semantics of the two are deliberately different, and the difference
   193	is inherited: `pr-review.yml:112-131` *fails* the code review when its token is
   194	missing, while `pr-review.yml:202-224` *skips* the prose review in the same
   195	situation.  Locally, a code reviewer that dies without output blocks the PR; a
   196	prose reviewer that dies leaves a warning and the code verdict stands.
   197	
   198	The published verdict takes the **worst** of the two lanes, written verbatim on
   199	the `VERDICT:` line of one exact-head `COMMENT` review (marker
   200	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`): `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED` or
   201	`CHANGES_REQUESTED`.  Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT` too; adverseness lives
   202	in the paired `local-review/summary` status, `success` only for `APPROVED` or a
   203	`COMMENTED` verdict with an empty ledger and `failure` otherwise.  A head with
   204	no review at all simply has no such status, which the merge gate reads as
   205	"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.
   206	
   207	## 8. Concurrency
   208	
   209	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   212	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   213	
   214	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   215	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   216	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   217	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   218	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   219	
   220	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   221	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
   222	is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
   223	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
   224	invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
   225	describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
   226	the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
   227	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   228	
   229	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   230	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   231	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   232	rewritten under it.
   233	
   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   248	
   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   250	|---|---|---|
   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   268	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   269	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   270	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   271	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   272	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   273	A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
   274	`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
   275	because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
   276	2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
   277	adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
   278	watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.
   279	
   280	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   281	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   282	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   283	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   284	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   285	
   286	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   287	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   288	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   289	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   290	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   291	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.
   292	
   293	## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`
   294	
   295	`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
   296	`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
   297	`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
   298	proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
   299	branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
   300	validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
   301	(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
   302	
   303	The local translation is:
   304	
   305	| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
   306	|---|---|---|
   307	| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   308	| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   309	| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |
   310	
   311	`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
   312	responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
   313	comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
   314	that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
   315	`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
   316	refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
   317	is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
   318	collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.
   319	
   320	The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
   321	running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
   322	survives as a lint in all three scripts.
   323	
   324	`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
   325	`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
   326	reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
   327	session used one anyway.
   328	
   329	The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
   330	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   331	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   332	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).

   362	## 5. Review Checklist
   363	
   364	Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:
   365	
   366	1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   367	   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.
   368	
   369	2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   370	   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   371	   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.
   372	
   373	3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   374	   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   375	   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   376	   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   377	   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   378	   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   379	   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   380	   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   381	   under [audits/](../audits/).
   382	   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   383	   format in
   384	   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).
   385	   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   386	   public name.
   387	   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   388	   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   389	   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   390	   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.
   391	
   392	4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   393	   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   394	   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   395	   exception policy.
   396	
   397	5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   398	   metavariables.
   399	
   400	6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   401	   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.
   402	
   403	7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   404	   upstreamed to Mathlib?
   405	
   406	8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   407	   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   408	   relevant arXiv paper(s).
   409	
   410	9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   411	   from the blueprint, add `\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\leanok` tags to the
   412	   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public
   413	   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record
   414	   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only
   415	   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal
   416	   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected
   417	   by `\uses{...}`. See
   418	   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).
   419	   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or
   420	   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
   421	   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,
   422	   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,
   423	   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional
   424	   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before
   425	   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as
   426	   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been
   427	   formalized.
   428	
   429	10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded
   430	   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that
   431	   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom
   432	   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See
   433	   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and
   434	   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.
   435	
   436	11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against
   437	   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure
   438	   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail
   439	   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),
   440	   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches
   441	   hiding preconditions (A3), trivial default witnesses (A4),
   442	   Mathlib-bypass castles (A5), and external `*Statement` smuggles (A6).
   443	   Use the reviewer checklist at the end of that file.
   444	
   445	12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure
   446	   fields such as `*Input`, `*Residual`, `*BridgeInputs`, `*Witness`,
   447	   `*Statement`, `*Conclusion`, or `*Package`, review it against

    45	## 2. Evidence contracts
    46	
    47	All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).
    48	
    49	**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
    50	`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
    51	`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
    52	`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
    53	`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
    54	after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
    55	the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
    56	status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
    57	PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
    58	`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.
    59	
    60	**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
    61	carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
    62	line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
    63	Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
    64	`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
    65	too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
    66	event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
    67	(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.
    68	
    69	**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
    70	`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
    71	line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.
    72	
    73	**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
    74	read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
    75	it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
    76	webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.

    78	## 3. The merge gate
    79	
    80	`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
    81	never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
    82	`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
    83	commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
    84	that refuse by default:
    85	
    86	1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
    87	   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
    88	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
    89	   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
    90	3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
    91	   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
    92	   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    93	4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per
    94	   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
    95	   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
    96	   `success` there;
    97	5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
    98	6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);
    99	   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix
   100	   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;
   101	7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
   102	   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.
   103	
   104	`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
   105	an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.
   106	
   107	Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
   108	remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
   109	dirt defers it with a warning).
   110	
   111	## 4. Untrusted text
   112	
   113	Issue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive
   114	from GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,
   115	writes the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into
   116	agent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and
   117	`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced
   118	code with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for
   119	bodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).
   120	
   121	Every LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on
   122	`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != "false"`; read prompts from committed main
   123	(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame
   124	sanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed
   125	label through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally
   126	keeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.
   127	
   128	## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive
   129	
   130	`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local
   131	location); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read
   132	from the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s
   133	own loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with
   134	the reason recorded in `results/telemetry/events.md`, unlike
   135	`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE` (the pre-commit budget), the one owner-gated control
   136	in the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and
   137	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).
   138	
   139	`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only
   140	snapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`
   141	(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the
   142	issue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The
   143	retired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit
   144	c8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.

docs/reports/issue-930-session47-commutativity-audit.md:62:The proof route is the paper route after the already documented scalar/tensor public-interface choice from `docs/paper-gaps/issue-713-scalar-tensor-decision.tex`: the evaluated commutation estimate is first specialized to evaluated questions (`evaluationSpecialization_sddErrorOp_eq`), then the full-slice products are transported back by the two Schwartz--Zippel marginalization steps (`Main/EvaluatedQuestions.lean:27-46`). docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:179:**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:198:**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

   334	## 11. Operating it
   335	
   336	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   337	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   338	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   339	
   340	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   341	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   342	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   343	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   344	neither publishes a review.

   346	Artefacts:
   347	
   348	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   349	|---|---|---|
   350	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   351	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   352	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |

   355	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so

   359	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear

   362	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   363	agreeing is intentional redundancy.

   365	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses

   370	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   371	
   372	Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".
   373	
   374	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   375	  One reviewer session; the cascade

   377	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   378	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   379	  comes from a branch of this single repository.

   381	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.

   390	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   391	
   392	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   393	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   394	
   395	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   396	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   397	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   398	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   399	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   400	   `moot: <reason>`);
   401	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   402	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   403	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   404	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   405	
   406	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   407	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   408	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   409	
   410	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   411	
   412	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   413	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   414	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   415	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   416	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   417	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   418	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
   419	and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
   420	from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
   421	review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
   422	`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
   423	are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
   424	change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
   425	patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

   362	## 5. Review Checklist
   363	
   364	Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:
   365	
   366	1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   367	   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.
   368	
   369	2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   370	   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   371	   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.
   372	
   373	3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   374	   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   375	   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   376	   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   377	   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   378	   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   379	   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   380	   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   381	   under [audits/](../audits/).
   382	   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   383	   format in
   384	   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).
   385	   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   386	   public name.
   387	   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   388	   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   389	   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   390	   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.
   391	
   392	4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   393	   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   394	   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   395	   exception policy.
   396	
   397	5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   398	   metavariables.
   399	
   400	6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   401	   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.
   402	
   403	7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   404	   upstreamed to Mathlib?
   405	
   406	8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   407	   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   408	   relevant arXiv paper(s).
   409	
   410	9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   411	   from the blueprint, add `\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\leanok` tags to the
   412	   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public
   413	   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record
   414	   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only
   415	   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal
   416	   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected
   417	   by `\uses{...}`. See
   418	   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).
   419	   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or
   420	   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
   421	   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,
   422	   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,
   423	   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional
   424	   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before
   425	   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as
   426	   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been
   427	   formalized.
   428	
   429	10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded
   430	   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that
   431	   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom
   432	   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See
   433	   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and
   434	   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.
   435	
   436	11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against
   437	   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure
   438	   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail
   439	   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),
   440	   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches

   444	
   445	12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure

1	# Protocol: issues and pull requests
     2	
     3	Normative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in
     4	`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is
     5	`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for
     6	issues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*
     7	here and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no
     8	shadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error
     9	fails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).
    10	
    11	## 1. Records, names, tools
    12	
    13	Issues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,
    14	no frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation
    15	(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the
    16	retired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the
    17	repository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a
    18	label absent from GitHub is reported, never invented. Briefs (the design record
    19	per issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.
    20	
    21	Every GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python
    22	callers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,
    23	`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,
    24	`issue-create`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists them) owning CLI
    25	discovery, repository resolution, API version headers, bounded retry of
    26	transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention. Nothing else shells
    27	out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`, `ci.sh`,
    28	`review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub numbers;
    29	`track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.
    30	
    31	* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`
    32	  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.
    33	* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch
    34	  names inherit those characters and "`]` breaks part of the PR automation
    35	  stack" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine
    36	  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.
    37	* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes
    38	  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the
    39	  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain
    40	  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.
    41	* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does
    42	  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that
    43	  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.
    44	
    45	## 2. Evidence contracts
    46	
    47	All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).
    48	
    49	**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
    50	`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
    51	`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
    52	`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
    53	`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
    54	after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
    55	the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
    56	status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
    57	PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
    58	`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.
    59	
    60	**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
    61	carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
    62	line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
    63	Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
    64	`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
    65	too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
    66	event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
    67	(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.
    68	
    69	**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
    70	`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
    71	line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.
    72	
    73	**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
    74	read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
    75	it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
    76	webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.
    77	
    78	## 3. The merge gate
    79	
    80	`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
    81	never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
    82	`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
    83	commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
    84	that refuse by default:
    85	
    86	1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
    87	   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
    88	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
    89	   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
    90	3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
    91	   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
    92	   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    93	4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per
    94	   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
    95	   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
    96	   `success` there;
    97	5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
    98	6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);
    99	   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix
   100	   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;
   101	7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
   102	   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.
   103	
   104	`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
   105	an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.
   106	
   107	Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
   108	remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
   109	dirt defers it with a warning).
   110	
   111	## 4. Untrusted text
   112	
   113	Issue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive
   114	from GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,
   115	writes the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into
   116	agent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and
   117	`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced
   118	code with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for
   119	bodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).

   121	Every LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on
   122	`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != "false"`; read prompts from committed main
   123	(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame
   124	sanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed
   125	label through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally
   126	keeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.
   127	
   128	## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive
   129	
   130	`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local
   131	location); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read
   132	from the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s

   137	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).

   139	`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3

     3	
     4	The one script in the issue-lifecycle area that changes ``main``: the local
     5	replacement for GitHub's branch-protection rules, which upstream were server-side
     6	settings no client could bypass.  A single-account repository has none — the owner can
     7	always press Merge — so the authority is this file.  It refuses by default, every
     8	override is named, and ``gh_common.merge_pr`` merges through the REST ``sha`` guard,
     9	which makes GitHub reject the call if the head moved meanwhile.
    10	
    11	Every piece of evidence lives on GitHub, bound to the head SHA (issues-prs.md; the old
    12	``prs/`` registry is archived under ``results/telemetry/registry-archive/``):
    13	
    14	1. the PR is open, unmerged, not a draft;
    15	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip is that
    16	   SHA — the merge must be of the bytes that were built here;
    17	3. the eight ``local-ci/<step>`` contexts (ci.sh:70) and ``local-ci/summary`` are
    18	   ``success`` on it.  A missing context blocks: GitHub's combined state reads
    19	   "success" for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    20	4. a ``<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`` COMMENT review sits on that exact
    21	   commit id, its ``VERDICT:`` line is APPROVED (or COMMENTED with zero unchecked
    22	   findings), and ``local-review/summary`` is ``success`` (DESIGN.md:66-69) — one
    23	   account cannot self-APPROVE, so an adverse verdict travels in that status;
    24	5. no ``CHANGES_REQUESTED`` review sits on that SHA, from anyone;
    25	6. the fix loop is quiescent: no live autofix.sh lock.  The ``[codex-auto-fix]`` /
    26	   ``[codex-review-fix]`` commit count since the merge base is printed for the
    27	   record only — the iteration cap is autofix.sh's loop-termination bound and
    28	   carries no merge authority (issues-prs.md 3; EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-02);

    32	``ADJUDICATION`` comment names this exact head (review.md 12).  GitHub merges and
    33	closes the linked issues itself, so no local bookkeeping can double-count.  The

   121	def ensure_mergeable_worktree(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> None:
   122	    """Gate 2 — clean primary worktree on the base, local branch at the head.
   123	
   124	    GitHub performs the merge, so none of this is needed for the merge itself; all of it
   125	    is needed for the tail, which fast-forwards ``base`` in this very worktree and
   126	    deletes the branch.  Refusing here keeps the failure before the irreversible step.
   127	    """
   128	    dirty = git(repo_root, "status", "--porcelain")
   129	    if dirty:
   130	        raise GateFailure("gate 2 (worktree): the primary tree is not clean, required clean "
   131	                          "so the post-merge fast-forward cannot lose work:\n" + dirty)
   132	    current = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
   133	    if current != base:
   134	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (worktree): HEAD is on {current!r}, required {base!r} "
   135	                          f"(the PR base). Run: git switch {base}")
   136	    tip = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{branch}^{{commit}}", check=False)
   137	    if not tip:
   138	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (local branch): {branch!r} does not resolve here, required "
   139	                          f"it at {head_sha[:12]}: git fetch github {branch}:{branch}")
   140	    if tip != head_sha:
   141	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (local branch): {branch} tip is {tip[:12]}, required "
   142	                          f"{head_sha[:12]} (the PR head). Push or fetch — the evidence binds "
   143	                          "to the SHA, not to the branch name.")
   144	    passed(f"gate 2 worktree clean on {base}, local tip == head")

   147	def check_ci(statuses: dict, head_sha: str) -> None:
   148	    """Gate 3 — every CI context is ``success`` on the exact head SHA."""
   149	    problems: list[str] = []
   150	    for context in CI_CONTEXTS:
   151	        row = statuses.get(context)
   152	        if row is None:
   153	            problems.append(f"{context}: MISSING")
   154	        elif row.get("state") != "success":
   155	            problems.append(f"{context}: {row.get('state')} "
   156	                            f"({sanitize(str(row.get('description') or ''), 120)})")
   157	    if problems:
   158	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 3 (CI): required success on {head_sha[:12]} for all "
   159	                          f"{len(CI_CONTEXTS)} contexts; observed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(problems)
   160	                          + "\nRun local/bin/ci.sh on this head. A missing context is a block, "
   161	                          "never a pass: GitHub's combined state is 'success' for a commit "
   162	                          "with no statuses at all.")
   163	    passed(f"gate 3 all {len(CI_CONTEXTS)} local-ci contexts success")

   166	def check_review(repo_root: Path, number: int, head_sha: str, reviews: list[dict],
   167	                 statuses: dict, *, adjudicated: bool) -> set[int]:
   168	    """Gate 4 — one verdict review on this commit id, clean or adjudicated."""
   169	    marker = f"<!-- mipstarre-review pr={number} head={head_sha} -->"
   170	    matching = [r for r in reviews
   171	                if r.get("commit_id") == head_sha and marker in (r.get("body") or "")]
   172	    if not matching:
   173	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): no review carrying {marker} on commit "
   174	                          f"{head_sha[:12]}, required exactly one. A verdict on an earlier SHA "
   175	                          "does not carry over (DESIGN.md:66-69): re-run review.sh.")
   176	    # One verdict review per head is the contract; if a retry ever leaves two, the newest
   177	    # is operative (the API returns reviews in creation order).
   178	    body = matching[-1].get("body") or ""
   179	    found = VERDICT_RE.search(body)
   180	    verdict = found.group(1) if found else ""
   181	    unchecked = len(UNCHECKED_FINDING_RE.findall(body))
   182	    summary_state = (statuses.get(REVIEW_CONTEXT) or {}).get("state")
   183	    # Green needs BOTH a clean verdict and a clean ledger: an APPROVED trailer
   184	    # over unresolved findings is inconsistent reviewer output (round 2, F4).
   185	    clean = verdict in ("APPROVED", "COMMENTED") and unchecked == 0
   186	    if clean and summary_state == "success":
   187	        passed(f"gate 4 verdict {verdict} on {head_sha[:12]}, {REVIEW_CONTEXT} success")
   188	        return set()
   189	    observed = (f"VERDICT {verdict or 'absent'} with {unchecked} unchecked finding(s), "
   190	                f"{REVIEW_CONTEXT} {summary_state or 'MISSING'}")
   191	    if not adjudicated:
   192	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): required VERDICT APPROVED, or COMMENTED with zero "
   193	                          f"unchecked findings, and {REVIEW_CONTEXT} success; observed "
   194	                          f"{observed}. Address the findings (or tick them off with a reason and "
   195	                          "a tracked issue) and re-run review.sh, or merge --adjudicated.")
   196	    # review.md section 12: past the round cap the operator may adjudicate what is left.
   197	    # A round is a marker review bound to the head it names and not itself a
   198	    # carried copy (review.md section 13): carried bodies and unbound markers
   199	    # never count towards adjudication eligibility.
   200	    round_marker = re.compile(rf"mipstarre-review pr={number} head=([0-9a-f]{{40}})")
   201	    reviewed_heads = {m.group(1) for row in reviews
   202	                      if (m := round_marker.search(row.get("body") or ""))
   203	                      and row.get("commit_id") == m.group(1)
   204	                      and "mipstarre-review-carried" not in (row.get("body") or "")}
   205	    if not reviewed_heads - {head_sha}:
   206	        raise GateFailure("gate 4 (review): adjudication is available after two review rounds; "
   207	                          "no prior reviewed head was found.")
   208	    finding_ids = UNCHECKED_ID_RE.findall(body)
   209	    if len(finding_ids) != unchecked or len(set(finding_ids)) != unchecked:
   210	        raise GateFailure("gate 4 (review): every unresolved finding must have one unique F<n> "
   211	                          "identifier before it can be adjudicated.")
   212	    accepted = None
   213	    for row in gh_common.api(f"issues/{number}/comments", paginate=True):
   214	        text = (row.get("body") or "").lstrip()
   215	        heads = HEAD_FIELD_RE.findall(text)
   216	        dispositions = DISPOSITION_RE.findall(text)
   217	        disposition_ids = [match[0] for match in dispositions]
   218	        if (text.startswith("ADJUDICATION") and heads == [head_sha]
   219	                and sorted(disposition_ids) == sorted(finding_ids)
   220	                and len(set(disposition_ids)) == len(disposition_ids)):
   221	            accepted = (row, dispositions)
   222	            break
   223	    if accepted is None:
   224	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): --adjudicated given but no ADJUDICATION comment "
   225	                          f"on PR #{number} has exactly head={head_sha} and one checked, valid "
   226	                          f"disposition for each of {unchecked} unresolved finding(s).")
   227	    row, dispositions = accepted
   228	    # `fixed in <sha>` must name a commit that is part of this PR's history.
   229	    for fixed_sha in re.findall(r"fixed in ([0-9a-f]{7,40})", row.get("body") or ""):
   230	        reachable = subprocess.run(
   231	            ["git", "-C", str(repo_root), "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", fixed_sha, head_sha],
   232	            capture_output=True).returncode == 0
   233	        if not reachable:
   234	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): disposition 'fixed in {fixed_sha}' does not name a commit "
   235	                              f"reachable from the PR head {head_sha[:12]}")
   236	    for _, issue_number in dispositions:
   237	        if not issue_number:
   238	            continue
   239	        issue = gh_common.api(f"issues/{issue_number}")
   240	        if issue.get("pull_request") or issue.get("state") != "open":
   241	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): deferred issue #{issue_number} does not exist "
   242	                              "as an open tracked issue.")
   243	    where = str(row.get("html_url") or row.get("id"))
   244	    sys.stderr.write(f"warning: merging PR #{number} on operator adjudication ({where}); the "
   245	                     f"review evidence is adverse — {observed}\n")
   246	    passed(f"gate 4 adjudicated at {head_sha[:12]} ({where})")
   247	    return {int(issue_number) for _, issue_number in dispositions if issue_number}

   250	def check_fix_gates(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> str:
   251	    """Gate 6 — refuse while the serialized fix loop is mid-flight.
   252	    Returns the merge base (gate 7 scans the same commit range); the fix-prefixed
   253	    commit count is reported, never enforced (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-02)."""

   255	    # locks/fix-<branch with / -> ->.lock, holder pid in <lock>/pid).  Probe the same lock
   256	    # the same way; a dead holder's lock does not block the merge.
   257	    lock = lock_dir() / ("fix-" + branch.replace("/", "-") + ".lock")
   258	    if lock.is_dir():
   259	        pid_text = ""
   260	        try:
   261	            pid_text = (lock / "pid").read_text(encoding="ascii").split()[0]
   262	        except (OSError, IndexError):
   263	            pass
   264	        if pid_text.isdigit() and _pid_alive(int(pid_text)):
   265	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 6 (fix loop): {lock} is held by live pid {pid_text}, required "
   266	                              "idle. autofix.sh is rewriting this branch and merging under it "
   267	                              "would race the fix commits.")
   268	    base_ref = None
   269	    for candidate in (f"github/{base}", f"refs/remotes/origin/{base}", base):
   270	        if git_ok(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{candidate}^{{commit}}"):

   272	            break
   273	    if base_ref is None:
   274	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): no local ref resolves for base {base!r}, so "
   275	                          f"the merge-base commit range cannot be scanned. Run: git fetch "
   276	                          f"github {base}")
   277	    merge_base = git(repo_root, "merge-base", base_ref, head_sha)
   278	    # `git rev-list --format` prints a "commit <sha>" header before each formatted line.
   279	    lines = git(repo_root, "rev-list", "--format=%s", f"{merge_base}..{head_sha}").splitlines()

   281	                     and line.startswith(FIX_COMMIT_PREFIXES))
   282	    passed(f"gate 6 fix loop idle; {iterations} fix-prefixed commit(s) since "
   283	           f"{merge_base[:12]} (autofix.sh bounds its own loop)")
   284	    return merge_base

   287	def check_dependencies(repo_root: Path, number: int, body: str,

   345	                          "into the branch, re-run CI and review on the new head, then merge.")

    84	## Scope control (added 2026-09-01 after the issue-0007 overbuild)
    85	
    86	The product is the Lean formalization; `local/` is scaffolding, and
    87	scaffolding work is a COST, not an achievement.  Binding rules:
    88	
    89	- Budget: a workflow change defaults to ≤2 hours wall time and ≤400 changed
    90	  lines.  Reaching either limit means stop, commit what stands, record the
    91	  state in telemetry, and escalate to the owner with a concrete question —
    92	  never push through the ceiling.  The pre-commit hook checks the line budget
    93	  per commit; the episode total is the PR diff, which the review checks.
    94	- Hooks stay under 60 seconds; heavier checks belong to CI steps.
    95	- No new abstraction layers (API clients, lock managers, frameworks) and no
    96	  rewrite of working, reviewed code without an explicit owner directive.
    97	  Prefer the smallest diff that satisfies the brief; prefer `gh` and the REST
    98	  API over reimplementation; prefer configuring GitHub once over re-verifying
    99	  its settings on every operation.
   100	- After a workflow change merges, the next dispatched work item MUST be
   101	  mathematics.  Two consecutive workflow-only episodes require owner approval.
   102	- Queue discipline (events.md 2026-09-03, the eight-hour stall): at the start
   103	  of EVERY loop iteration, merge every PR that is CI-green and review-green on
   104	  its exact head before touching anything else.  A workflow-layer PR gets at
   105	  most two review rounds, then adjudication at its current head (the owner's
   106	  watchdog flags a third round as churn; mathematics PRs keep the four-round
   107	  cap of review.md §12).  Never grow a PR to satisfy findings — the line budget is a
   108	  ceiling, not a target; a PR that has grown past twice its original size is
   109	  reset to its original head.  Findings that ask for new mechanisms are
   110	  dispositioned "out of scope" in the adjudication, not turned into issues.
   111	- When you notice yourself hardening the hardening (a fix whose only consumer
   112	  is another fix), stop and report — that pattern cost this project 17 hours
   113	  on 2026-09-01 (events.md).
   114	- The ONLY owner-gated control is `MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE`.  Every other
   115	  parameter, flag and gate remedy — `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`, `--adjudicated`,
   116	  `--force-review`, the `MIPSTARRE_CI_*` knobs, ticking a finding with a

   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   268	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   269	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   270	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   271	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   272	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   273	
   274	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   275	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   276	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   277	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   278	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   279	
   280	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   281	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   282	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   283	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   284	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   285	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

   287	## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`
   288	
   289	`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
   290	`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
   291	`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
   292	proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
   293	branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
   294	validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
   295	(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
   296	
   297	The local translation is:
   298	
   299	| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
   300	|---|---|---|
   301	| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   302	| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   303	| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |
   304	
   305	`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
   306	responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
   307	comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
   308	that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
   309	`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
   310	refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
   311	is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
   312	collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.
   313	
   314	The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
   315	running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
   316	survives as a lint in all three scripts.
   317	
   318	`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
   319	`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
   320	reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
   321	session used one anyway.
   322	
   323	The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
   324	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   325	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   326	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).
   327	
   328	## 11. Operating it
   329	
   330	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   331	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   332	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   333	
   334	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   335	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   336	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   337	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   338	neither publishes a review.
   339	
   340	Artefacts:
   341	
   342	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   343	|---|---|---|
   344	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   345	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   346	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   347	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   348	
   349	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   350	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   351	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   352	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   353	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   354	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   355	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   356	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   357	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   358	
   359	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   360	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   361	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   362	not a verdict.
   363	
   364	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   365	
   366	Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".
   367	
   368	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   369	  One reviewer session; the cascade
   370	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
   371	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   372	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   373	  comes from a branch of this single repository.
   374	* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
   375	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
   376	* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
   377	  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
   378	  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
   379	  allow-list only approximated.
   380	* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
   381	  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).
   382	
   383	
   384	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   385	
   386	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   387	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   388	
   389	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   390	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   391	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   392	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   393	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   394	   `moot: <reason>`);
   395	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   396	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   397	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   398	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   399	
   400	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   401	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   402	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   403	
   404	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   405	
   406	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   407	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   408	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   409	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   410	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   411	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   412	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
   413	and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
   414	from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
   415	review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
   416	`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
   417	are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
   418	change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
   419	patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

# Local operations — operator guide

This directory is the operative workflow of the repository: the local
replacement for the parent project's GitHub Actions layer. Architecture and
invariants: [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md). Protocol changes: follow
[`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md).

## The lifecycle at a glance

```
issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh
```

1. **File an issue**: `local/bin/issue_new.py --title "..." --body-file b.md --label ...` opens
   a GitHub issue and prints its number; `--parent N` attaches it as a native
   sub-issue. The brief for it goes in `local/briefs/`.
2. **Open a PR**: create branch `issue-<number>-slug`, worktree under
   `.worktrees/`, run `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` there, then
   `local/bin/pr_open.py --branch issue-<number>-slug --title "..." --body-file pr.md --issue N` (the body follows the PR template in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`),
   which pushes the branch and opens the GitHub PR.
3. **Dispatch agents**: only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover
   --issue NNNN --worktree .worktrees/<name> -- "task"`. Session telemetry
   lands in `results/telemetry/`.
4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
   `local/bin/site.sh all`.

## Ground rules for agents

- Read `AGENTS.md` first; the faithfulness policy and proof-integrity
  blockers are unchanged from the parent project.
- Never run `lake update`. Never write to the hot cache. Full `lake build`
  goes through the machine-wide lock (`warm-worktree.sh`/`ci.sh` handle it).
- One session never reviews its own diff.
- Sessions are dispatched, resumed, and archived only via `dispatch.sh`.
- Invoke workflow tools through the primary checkout's path
  (`/…/MIPStarRE-dev/local/bin/…`), never through a worktree's copy — a
  branch's copy can predate protocol fixes (EVOLUTION.md, 2026-08-30).
- Friction with any protocol → log it in `results/telemetry/events.md`;
  propose amendments per `protocols/meta.md`.

docs/blueprint_style_guide.md-177-**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md-178-
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:179:**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).

Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `local/protocols/review.md:273` — The new exception still conflicts with §12’s unqualified four-round threshold and issue-backed adjudication contract
- [ ] F2 (changes) `local/protocols/review.md:274` — Classifying all of `docs/` as workflow-only subjects mathematical paper-gap work to the shortened review path
- [ ] F3 (changes) `local/personas/main.md:103` — CI-green and review-green are insufficient merge criteria because five other authoritative gates can still block the PR

## Review

F1: The added paragraph says workflow-only PRs are adjudicated after round two, while the actual round-cap section at lines 390–406 still says every PR receives four rounds and every remaining finding is fixed or converted to an issue. The main persona likewise retains the four-round/tracked-issue rule at lines 52–55 but newly permits untracked `out of scope` dispositions at lines 104–110. `pr_merge.py` already accepts two-round and untracked out-of-scope adjudication, so the authoritative section and persona summaries should be updated to state that policy consistently. The duplicate `## 12` headings also make the new §12 references ambiguous.

F2: `docs/` contains mathematical artifacts such as `docs/paper-gaps/`, whose review affects source faithfulness; `local/bin/ci.sh:635` explicitly treats that directory as paper-gap material. Narrow the workflow-only definition to workflow-specific documentation rather than the entire tree.

F3: `local/protocols/issues-prs.md:86–105` requires seven merge gates. A reviewed, green PR may still be draft, lack a fresh base, have a mismatched local tip, race a fix lock, carry `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, or close an issue with open children. The queue rule should prioritize invoking `pr_merge.py` for candidates that pass all gates, not describe CI and review as sufficient.

Prior-ledger triage: the earlier `review.sh` refusal, counting, locking, rename, bot/force, duplication, and regression-test findings are resolved because that executable change was withdrawn. The earlier persona/protocol conflict remains as F1; the `docs/` classification remains as F2; and the incomplete merge predicate remains as F3.

The authoritative 65-line patch was read in full without truncation. `git diff --check` passes; no runtime tests were rerun because this head changes documentation/persona files only and the supplied exact-head CI trigger is green.
